summary: Jonathan Duquette is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD from Université de Montréal (2005–2011). He held fellowships at Oxford (2015–2019) and Birmingham (2020–2021), and was an affiliated lecturer and research associate at Cambridge in 2019.

Jonathan Edelmann is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford by 2009 and served as an assistant professor at the University of Florida in 2015.

Jonathan Geen, an Indologist and scholar of religious studies, completed his doctorate under Phyllis Granoff at McMaster University by 2001. He has taught at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover is a philosopher who studied at Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1960–1963). He was a fellow and tutor at New College (~1967–1998), taught at King's College London (~1998–2013), and held fellowships at Oxford and the Hastings Center.

Jonathan Lear (1948–2025) was a philosopher who earned degrees from Yale, Cambridge, and Rockefeller University (PhD 1978). He taught at Yale, Cambridge, and Clare College, before serving as a distinguished service professor at the University of Chicago (2014–2022).

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1970–1983), working under George F. Dales (~1974–1983), and became a professor of anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 1985.

Jonathan Scott (1754–1829) was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian scholar who co-founded The Asiatic Society. He served as professor of oriental languages at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1802) and the East India Company College (~1802–1805).

Jonathan Z. Smith (1938–2017) was a religious studies scholar educated at Haverford and Yale. He taught at Dartmouth and UC Santa Barbara, served as Dean of the College at the University of Chicago (1977–1982), and presided over the SBL (2008).

Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Shitennoji University and the University of Hamburg, completing his PhD by 1998 under Lambert Schmithausen, alongside studies under S. A. Srinivasan, A. Wezler, and D. Seyfort Ruegg.

Jongcheol Lee is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Seoul National University and completed a PhD at the University of Tokyo (1994) under Yasunori Ejima. He was a researcher at Mysore (1992) and associate professor at AKS (2001).

Jongmyung Kim is a Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies scholar who studied at Yonsei, Seoul National University, and UCLA (MA by 1994 under Robert E. Buswell Jr.). He was associate professor at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

Joryu Chiba (1921–2008) was a Buddhist studies, Japanese history, and Japanology scholar educated at Ryukoku University. He held academic posts there from 1950 onward, including professor emeritus (1970–1989), and directed multiple Buddhist research institutes.

Jos Gommans is a historian and Indologist. Educated at Radboud University and Leiden University, he completed his doctoral studies under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink (~1987–1993). He became an associate professor (1993) and full professor (2011) at Leiden.

Jos. Schrijnen (1869–1938) was a linguist who earned his PhD at KU Leuven (1891) and studied in Paris. He held professorships at Utrecht University (1912, 1921) and served as rector and ordinary professor at Radboud University Nijmegen (1923–1938).

Josef Baudiš (1883–1933) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Charles University (doctorate under Josef Zubatý) and Heidelberg. He served as a Privatdozent at Charles University (~1913–1924) and was appointed professor at Comenius University in 1924.

Josef Friedrich Kohl (1908–1998) was an Indologist who studied in Prague and completed his PhD at the University of Bonn (~1932–1937) under Willibald Kirfel. He was a Privatdozent at Bonn and Prague, and became an apl. Professor at Würzburg in 1957.

Josef Horovitz (1874–1931) was a religious studies and history scholar who earned his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin (1897) under Eduard Sachau. He was professor of Arabic at Aligarh (1907–1914) and professor at Frankfurt (1915).
Josef Jungmann (1773–1847) was a linguist who studied at Charles University in 1795 and later held a post there from around 1815 to 1847.

Josef Kohler (1849–1919) was a scholar of Indology and legal history. He studied at Heidelberg and the University of Freiburg (promotion ~1868–1873) and served as professor at the University of Würzburg (1878) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1888).

Josef Kuckertz (1930–1996) was an ethnomusicologist and Indologist who earned his PhD (1962) and habilitation (1967) at the University of Cologne. He became a professor of musicology at Cologne in 1970 and a professor at Free University of Berlin in 1980.
